newsitem.title: USA: Ford names Homer Neal as new board member.
newsitem.headline: Ford names Homer Neal as new board member.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday it elected Homer Neal, interim president of the University of Michigan, to its board of directors.
Neal's appointment will take effect January 1, 1997. As of March 1996, Ford had 15 directors on its board.

The 54-year-old Neal has been serving as interim president of the university, which last week named Lee Bollinger as its new president. Neal is expected to step down when Bollinger takes office, possibly in late February or early March.

After Ford's annual meeting in May 1996, two board members, Colby Chandler and Kenneth Olsen, retired, leaving the company with 13 current members. When Neal joins in January, Ford will have 14 directors.
In addition to his interim post, Neal is vice president for research of the university. Neal joined the University of Michigan as the chairman of its physics department in 1987.

"Technical expertise is vital to the success of our company and the board has acted to add a highly skilled technical person with a deep and thorough understanding of research and development," Ford Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alex Trotman said in a statement.
